rites.name: Rauntalles
rites.text: A fierce mark of the wild hunt, named for the battle-fury that a warband of tribal raiders takes up in its clan rites. The same savage spirit is also shown by rites that carry the fury without naming it.

rites.name: Ameornia
rites.text: A legendary spirit-caller of the great stone-hills, said to wander in from a realm beyond ours. Tribes speak of its dread-sowing rites with a mixture of awe and fear.

rites.name: Vireoles
rites.text: A bound craft that gathers a chosen band of beings under one shared pattern, so that all who share a kind answer to the same signs. Its followers arrange their gatherings around that common lineage.

rites.name: Serarnestia
rites.text: Serarnestia is the concept of a lone threshold-warden who keeps the sealed doors of Lyenora's Courts, judged in the age of trials when the first doorways between worlds were set. She is remembered as the voice that decides which passages stay open and which are closed forever.

rites.name: Brastornock
rites.text: Brastornock is the Concept of Lyenora's Courts, the sovereign principle of judgment that weighs every trial and seats each council before the doors between worlds are raised. It does not strike in anger but settles disputes by the simple weight of its verdict, which can unmake a warded hall in an instant.

rites.name: Iseistora
rites.text: Iseistora is a concept of Lyenora, the principle that a sworn word can be bent into a door between worlds during the Courts. It is most often invoked when councils must bind a grove to a kingdom's oath. Its power is measured in the stillness it leaves behind rather than in any visible blast.

rites.name: Gougurn
rites.text: Gougurn is an arcane concept of Lyenora, a doctrine of the Courts that names the weight a sworn oath carries when it is spoken at a door between worlds. In the Age of Sundering it was argued in councils as the reason landfall could be stopped, and its keepers are said to bind the seams of old bonds with it.

rites.name: Theizess
rites.text: Theizess is the concept of thresholds as they are tested, the principle that a door holds only if someone is willing to pass through it. In the Courts of Lyenora it is invoked whenever the builders of the doors between worlds must prove their work against the strain of landfall during the Age of Sundering.

rites.name: Tirnia
rites.text: A binding rite that fuses a beast spirit and a human spirit into one. Those who accept it become calm, obedient servants, and a few are fully freed from their affliction.

rites.name: Nesus
rites.text: A tactic of cards that hunt winged beasts, striking them down, stripping away their wings, or punishing those who keep them. The verdant practitioners wield it best.

rites.name: Telintes
rites.text: A binding practice where a keeper gathers their beasts into a single pact, granting them the right to share out harm taken in battle. Once joined, the pact also reshapes how the group charges and guards.

rites.name: Relium
rites.text: A class of rites that only quick charms and scrolls may carry, first recorded among the wandering spirit-folk of a distant realm. It foreshadows later rites shared by one kin.

rites.name: Risanum Telesaurus
rites.text: A set of five blessings, one for each hue of a sacred palette, each granting a benefit tied to the number three. More broadly, the term names any helpful favor or gift bestowed upon someone.

rites.name: Teleror
rites.text: A ritual craft that breathes life into a lifeless object or corpse, granting it a body that moves and acts for a set span of time. It was among the earliest workings of its kind recorded by the orders.

rites.name: Orerostanum
rites.text: A sorcerous rite that can be paid for in an alternate manner. When chosen, the caster's spell also brings a land under their command to life as a temporary elemental that gains lasting growth counters.

rites.name: Viarnines
rites.text: A ritual tally that measures how much scorching harm a bearer has taken or dealt under shifting conditions. Its readings are kept by temple keepers as a measure of burning force.

rites.name: Corostalles
rites.text: A binding craft in which one bearer sets aside a lesser presence and steps into its place, taking up the same post to fight on its behalf. The displaced presence is held away until the bond is broken.

rites.name: Orellanum
rites.text: A standing binding that keeps a bearer from ever striking outward. It holds the bearer back from offense while leaving it free to guard and block.

rites.name: Vasor
rites.text: A second way to pay for a working, offered in place of its usual price. Its first examples appeared among the sacrificial incantations of an old age.

rites.name: Sereornes
rites.text: A rarely invoked practice in which rivals offer a portion of their own vitality in exchange for a chosen benefit. The offer is made openly and is weighed against the reward sought.

rites.name: Corileontes
rites.text: A battle discipline that grants a warrior added strength whenever they stand against an enemy or are themselves confronted in combat.

rites.name: Mentus Meostialus
rites.text: A bearer that is singled out by a caster's chant gains a surge of strength whenever a spell is aimed at it. The caster gains lasting rewards each time such a spell touches the bearer.

rites.name: Telarontum
rites.text: A brief magical working that is cast and resolved at once, then discarded to its owner's pile. It never remains in place on the field once its effect has been completed.

rites.name: Telonum
rites.text: A mutual reckoning where two beings strike each other with force equal to their own strength. The ritual is favored by wild orders and tends to be fought in heated, brawling spirit.

rites.name: Veostium Corinor
rites.text: A discipline by which practitioners draw flame from their own bodies and command it with breath and motion. It is an inherited art tied to a particular people's lineage.

rites.name: Coraullor Orelum
rites.text: A grim discipline that makes a fighter impossible to stand against, save by constructs of pure craft or by warriors bearing the same mark of kin. Such a mark keeps rivals from barring its path.

rites.name: Amausum
rites.text: A set of sacred tests sits at the heart of a desert people's devotion. Their faith is built entirely around these proving rites.

rites.name: Vaulia
rites.text: A small marker that a healer's spirit companion sets aside to absorb harm, shielding a creature from being wounded.

rites.name: Veostum
rites.text: A small tokened gauge that a caster stacks as the waters rise around a battle. Its marks are tied to wet, rushing effects that hinge on how many have gathered.

rites.name: Riasteonium
rites.text: A ritual term used by scholars to describe a rite that halts every blow struck during one cycle of combat. Its practice wanders among several orders, passing from hand to hand before settling back among the green-robed keepers.

rites.name: Rines Tosinium
rites.text: A devotional count of sigils borne by a bearer, tallied in one of five hues. It measures how deeply a follower is bound to a chosen hue or pair of hues.

rites.name: Nauseolles
rites.text: A quiet barrier-passing art that lets a strike slip only past warriors who answer the call of swift feet. It serves as a method of evading defenders.

rites.name: Maurus
rites.text: A preserving rite that binds the spirit of a fallen warrior to a stored form. It draws its power from the colors of light and tide.

rites.name: Lornia
rites.text: A lasting magical working that stays bound to the world without fading. It persists in place for an indefinite span once it is set.

rites.name: Mostantus
rites.text: A forbidden ritual that drains the inner embers of far-wandering casters to lift one user toward godlike mastery. Its origin is lost, and seers recognize it as an ancient, primal working.

rites.name: Valenum Velia
rites.text: A keyword marking a crafted power that a dragon-kin clan of the red and green lineages depends on. It is shared among their warriors as their defining mark of strength.

rites.name: Telesium Serenium
rites.text: An unseen, colorless fire that a mighty sky-sage once unleashed against devouring beasts from beyond the world. Its ignition, together with the presence of three wandering mages, is said to awaken a sealed sacred relic.

rites.name: Mirnianum
rites.text: A bond between a rider and mount that lets the attacking beast pass only through foes sharing its own kind of stride. Lesser creatures cannot stand in its path.

rites.name: Cialleones
rites.text: A trigger that stirs a creature into fury whenever it is harmed, rousing it to act. It marks the fighting instincts of the great beasts bred by the sun-worshipping realm.

rites.name: Larum
rites.text: A basic binding craft used by casters to enslave lesser beings and seize full command over them. A sufficiently resolute mind can weaken or shatter the hold.

rites.name: Veosiantum
rites.text: A marker kind that gathers one more mark each turn as a bearer sinks deeper into a shared downward decline. Each mark adds a growing pull to the bearer's power.

rites.name: Amoraunanum
rites.text: A calling that marks beings who, when faced with peril or while weak, show bravery and willingly give themselves up for a larger cause.

rites.name: Neornus Montilium
rites.text: A lone warrior who marches forward unaccompanied grows stronger with each blessing that the bearer's allies have raised across the field. The more such blessings are standing, the greater the boost.

rites.name: Serialum
rites.text: A sub-kind of incantation found only on quick and sudden workings. It arrived in a newer scholastic tradition and is tightly bound to the practice of instruction.

rites.name: Sereosia Amorauntium
rites.text: A practitioner calls a being out of another place and binds it to carry out their wishes. The method is an old craft, now regarded as outdated.

rites.name: Nornia Mentes
rites.text: A sky-born blessing that grants a bearer the power to hurl crackling storm-fire. It is counted among the five foremost gifts, and its strength reshaped how the arcane arts developed.

rites.name: Valirnialum
rites.text: A binding incantation handed down from a master to the first scholar of a floating sky-isle. It lets its user pronounce commands that the world is compelled to obey.

rites.name: Coreornanum
rites.text: A rare set of five swift rites that each alter a spell or fixture into a single chosen hue. Originally they were cast as sudden interruptions.

rites.name: Amenia
rites.text: An old binding craft that ties a creature's nature to the terrain it must rest upon. It is now carried out by spelling out its conditions in full wherever it is practiced.

rites.name: Sellintium
rites.text: A legendary illusion that clouds the senses of those who meet it. It is said to be woven in a distant realm of the wider world.

rites.name: Nauliastia
rites.text: A tactic where a creature is laid to rest in the grave, then roused back onto the field by a cheap, efficient incantation. It has been practiced since the earliest days of the old ways.

rites.name: Reonternus
rites.text: A cunning bargain-craft in which a caster presents a seductive proposal that others may accept, and it is found only in quick spells and sudden rites.

rites.name: Oralentia
rites.text: A shared collective awareness that binds a folk together so their minds act as one. It also appears as a mechanic that lets creatures of a common kind link their thoughts and act in unison.

rites.name: Oronium Tiniaria
rites.text: A rare pale enchantment that binds to a creature and shields it from one chosen hue of magic. Several such bindings were once common in the oldest sanctioned charm-books.

rites.name: Nasialia
rites.text: A plot of ground that can be tapped for an effect beyond simply yielding power. Its abilities can ruin standing structures, strengthen allied bearers, or draw down a foe's stores, often requiring the plot and its neighbors to be spent.

rites.name: Reorestia
rites.text: A quiet tapping-ground that yields a helpful effect rather than a burst of colored essence. Its gifts serve practical needs instead of pouring out many hues at once.

rites.name: Niasus
rites.text: A tally kept by healers that records harm already suffered, which can later be turned back into renewed living strength. It was first set down in the earliest scrolls of the old orders.

rites.name: Amostenus
rites.text: A slow, creeping craft in which a bite or strike carries a lethal sickness that spreads through any creature it touches. Older works record it as a common skill among wandering hunters.

rites.name: Molausia
rites.text: A ritual call that gathers a lone sworn fighter from the ranks of the common folk. Each summons conjures a single pale-armored guard who answers the caller's banner.

rites.name: Rillia
rites.text: A divine stillness falls when every celestial overseer is drawn away from the world of mortals. A watcher of distant horizons takes them all out of reach, halting their clashes that threatened to shatter the land.

rites.name: Vausteolia
rites.text: A ritual sweep that makes every bearer discard their held tokens and draw a fresh set, usually seven. Many ancient rites of this kind were carved in the red and blue halls of the old orders.

rites.name: Ryanneth
rites.text: Ryanneth is the concept of the Seeding in Lyenora, the moment the makers sow the Weave into the world and the quiet powers lie dormant beneath the temples of the Holy Age. It is remembered as a hush before flame, when orders first learned to bind the sleeping currents of the Arcane Realm.

rites.name: Tenvaleno
rites.text: Tenvaleno is a concept of Lyenora as its makers plant the Weave, when the quiet powers lie dormant beneath the surface of the world. In the Age of Sundering that followed landfall, the concept was split along old bonds, and its fragments still hum faintly where the Weave runs thinnest.

rites.name: Seornillor
rites.text: A small enchantment that returns a fresh charm to its caster as it works its modest effect. Such workings can be found in every school of practice.

rites.name: Amanes
rites.text: A binding craft that lets a spirit be cast as an enchantment clinging to another creature. The host gains the spirit's strength, endurance, and gifts while the bond holds.

rites.name: Nallium
rites.text: A tap-activated boon that lets a chosen creature gain temporary strength and toughness until the turn ends. It is a common way to support allies in combat.

rites.name: Rostanes
rites.text: Spells of three colors shatter enchanted relics and bound trinkets. Red and green cast them most often, while white casts them more widely, and green's versions often also break wards.

rites.name: Niarastia
rites.text: A fierce hunger that stirs within a creature whenever it strikes a foe in battle, causing it to swell with added strength. Each blow against an enemy adds lasting power to its frame.

rites.name: Sialornor
rites.text: A tactic where an attacker's ally strikes the sides of a foe, leaving any defender that opposes it weakened by a small penalty, unless that defender fights with the same tactic.

rites.name: Corianor
rites.text: A ritual action that lets a wielder repeat a chosen effect a second time. It is named after a lone sovereign who first mastered the practice.

rites.name: Nintiastus
rites.text: A ward that shields a bearer from being chosen as the aim of hostile enchantments and workings. Foes cast their magic around the protected one, which keeps it untouched by rival sorcery.

rites.name: Neoristium
rites.text: A keyword ability that lets a fallen card return from the grave as a fresh, embalmed copy. Its magic is most common among the pale and blue-robed orders, and it is tied to a sundered warband of reanimated soldiers preserved in sealing resin.

rites.name: Nolerus
rites.text: A dormant binding craft that has been debated by makers but never inscribed on any lasting artifact. It sends every marked token to a sealed void before the rite of drawing begins.

rites.name: Seraunasor
rites.text: A paired set of traits used to mark a creature as bound to either the light or the dark. Its state can shift between the two as the hours turn.

rites.name: Coraustor
rites.text: A bonded binding that lets a fortress be set against a stronghold the way a hand is set upon a tool. Its craft works like fastening a gear, though it anchors to a plot of earth instead of a living bearer.

rites.name: Lereoles
rites.text: A dark art in which a caster siphons the vitality from a foe, wounding them while mending the caster's own body. Most practitioners of the shadowed arts favor this sinister exchange.

rites.name: Valiastires
rites.text: A mind-clouding craft that a bearer may invoke, whose effects awaken when the bearer's hand grows bare of certain sorts of shaped sigils.

rites.name: Seonor Amianosum
rites.text: A ritual power that lets a fallen caster rise again from the burial grounds by paying a price of other remembered relics. Those who return this way may gain an extra blessing.

rites.name: Valaules
rites.text: A surge of unthinking battle-fury that seizes a warrior when they strike. It first stirred in the age of far-seeing oracles.

rites.name: Seontes
rites.text: A keyword describing a decaying faction's method of pulling discarded remains back from the graveyard into use. It marks a kind of rot-driven recovery favored by those who live among the dead.

rites.name: Ceorus
rites.text: A ritual craft in which a spell is sung once and then cast again each turn, its echoes growing a little stronger. Scholars debate what it means for a single incantation to be remembered as a legend.

rites.name: Ameollia
rites.text: A working that takes effect without drawing on the caster's reserve of power. It usually demands a different price, paid in another form.

rites.name: Lonteosium
rites.text: A scorching incantation that burns away whatever its caster chooses to spend. Its heat can strike several foes at once, making it prized by those who favor sweeping ruin.

rites.name: Teornilum
rites.text: A returning mark that lets a fallen creature rise again in a ghostly shape. It is tied to beings brought back from death as spirits.

rites.name: Cinestium
rites.text: A binding rule that limits which kind of charm-tether may be fixed to a target. The tether is a lasting mark that clings to the thing it touches.

rites.name: Coraustium
rites.text: A protective enchantment wrapped around an entire realm, raised by a single caster to keep outside wanderers of the planes from harming the land and the people who live there.

rites.name: Nolauntum
rites.text: A craft that reshapes the nature of a ground-bound place so it yields a different source of power. Practitioners favor it as a way to reach kinds of magic otherwise out of their reach in crowded lands.

rites.name: Cisastium
rites.text: A binding craft that compels an opposing guardian to meet any bearer marked by it. Guardians touched by the ward cannot choose to stand aside from them.

rites.name: Miallintum
rites.text: A human woman who wields fire magic. She once briefly proclaimed herself ruler of her realm.

rites.name: Corontor Oriasum
rites.text: A mystic technique in which casting or duplicating a quick incantation or a sorcerous spell triggers a further effect. Practitioners treat it as a recurring rhythm of arcane power.

rites.name: Caurenus
rites.text: A joining rite where two linked tokens held on a practitioner's reverse side fuse into a single, much larger token. It only works when the bearer holds the correct matching pair.

rites.name: Caustiaror
rites.text: A snare-craft that works only on quick, fleeting workings. It was first taught in a wild realm and later remembered in a stormy land.

rites.name: Melleostium
rites.text: A learned discipline that lets a creature grow stronger when it fights beside a larger companion. It can only be found within living beings.

rites.name: Sostia
rites.text: A tally of bravery that a bearer gathers, and each creature under the bearer's command grows slightly stronger for it.

rites.name: Teornium
rites.text: A quiet trait that lets a sentinel strike forward while keeping its guard raised. The watcher never has to lower its stance to take part in an assault.

rites.name: Orosantia
rites.text: A slow, creeping blight that a craft can pass into things. It was first set loose in an older age and later stirred again.

rites.name: Maria
rites.text: A dark enchantment that bolsters a chosen creature with grim vigor. Its depiction has stirred disapproval among pious observers toward the wider craft that produced it.

rites.name: Sornianum
rites.text: A temporary seizing craft in which a caster briefly takes command of a creature, freeing it to strike at once. Its users favor it for feeding fallen beasts to their own purposes.

rites.name: Ciania Neosus
rites.text: A deed by which a traveler descends into a hidden underground maze of rooms and chambers. It is tied to the cards that represent such labyrinthine delves.

rites.name: Naulor
rites.text: A binding quality that keeps a charm from being unmade by rival wards. Sages of the old halls write it plainly on the parchment: this charm cannot be unwound.

rites.name: Ciralia
rites.text: A practiced art in which a caster draws upon a hidden archive of lore to call forth a specific, sought-after rite from among the scrolls they carry.

rites.name: Meornantia
rites.text: A bound incantation that can only be called forth from the dead-ground once its anchored object has already been laid there. After it is spoken, it is cast out of the world entirely.

rites.name: Xaisteth
rites.text: Xaisteth is the concept of the Pact sworn in the Fall of Lyenora, the binding that held the broken worlds together after the Sundering. It is remembered in the groves and growing kingdoms of the first sovereign's age as the principle that a shattered thing may still keep its word. Its power is the stability of agreements rather than force of arms.

rites.name: Kalunamum
rites.text: Kalunamum is a concept of Lyenora that embodies the stillness between breaking and binding, invoked by the orders of the Holy Age as the principle behind the sworn Pact. Its doctrine holds that flame must be tended rather than unleashed, a teaching kept in the temples long after the Shards scattered.

rites.name: Mialum
rites.text: A bound effect that a bearer may call forth by surrendering a required toll, such as spent essence or a turning motion. It usually lives within a standing object, yet it can also be awakened from a resting place or a held token.

rites.name: Neostialor
rites.text: A paired arrangement in which one guardian beast lets a crafter repeat a shaping spell, so a single gathering of tokens swells into an overwhelming host. It was banned after dominating the trade for a half-cycle.

rites.name: Rilleosia
rites.text: A battle-craft of hurried assault, where a band of small, fierce fighters wears down rivals through steady, swift blows. Its practitioners aim to end contests before their foes can recover.

rites.name: Sistum
rites.text: A tally of exchange that must be surrendered before a charm or gift takes hold. Practitioners pay it in coin, blood, or labor whenever a rite or ability is called upon.

rites.name: Serollum
rites.text: A shared-burden craft where companions may contribute part of the cost when someone casts a working. The helper covers only the unspecified portion of the expense.

rites.name: Seorenum
rites.text: A tactic where a warrior may cast off a fighter from the hand to lend an attacker a fleeting surge of strength and hardiness matching that fighter's own. The surge also carries over any combat skills the discarded fighter possessed.

rites.name: Reollor
rites.text: A trading custom where a caster may surrender a bound relic, sigil, or conjured figure while invoking a spell, gaining an extra boon in exchange for the offering.

rites.name: Valarneonor
rites.text: A keyword marking that a card may be cast aside from the hand to trigger a lasting effect. It was first brought into the craft during a great gathering of remembered spirits.

rites.name: Reontornes
rites.text: A slow binding craft where a hoard of gleaming engines and sealed towers holds rivals in check. Each turn the foe must surrender one of their holdings while the caster recalls their grounds from the dust.

rites.name: Calles
rites.text: When a warrior charges into the fray, it stirs every other attacking ally to hit harder. It works like a mirror of a solitary champion's rallying blessing.

rites.name: Vinteres
rites.text: A counter-measure is a token of craft that undoes an opposing force before it can finish its work. Crafters judge these by how cheaply they can be cast and how many kinds of threat they can meet.

rites.name: Meornontes
rites.text: A tally mark that wears down a creature's strength by placing small drains upon it. Each mark steadily shrinks the creature's power and resilience.

rites.name: Tinolor
rites.text: A ritual of witnessing where a bearer chooses a number of their own holdings or shows that many matching items from hand. The act counts as a sworn sighting of a chosen quality.

rites.name: Sernor
rites.text: A spell of sudden ruin that clears every creature or structure of one kind from the field at once. It is usually wielded by sages of the pale craft and is held in rare regard.

rites.name: Coraustia
rites.text: A rare decree that lets one person direct every choice another person makes, extending command over a single holding to the whole individual and their deeds.

rites.name: Valiases
rites.text: A practice in which a card-caster lifts a spell from its resting place, sets it upon the waiting stack, and settles its fees so it may later take effect.

rites.name: Cirernum
rites.text: A bound craft that lets engineered conveyances take on a living guise for a single turn. Those machines can then act as animated creatures until the turn ends.

rites.name: Seriales
rites.text: A craft of reinforcing allies by a small mark of strength, first taught to a mountain order and later shared with a sky clan. It also appears briefly on loose adhesive tokens.

rites.name: Teleoronia
rites.text: A practiced method by which a caster peers at the uppermost few sealed scrolls of their archive and draws one that fits a chosen category. The custom began with a verdant rite of old forest-wardens.

rites.name: Tisornum
rites.text: A recurring mechanic in which a holder sheds cards from their hand and sends them into a resting pile. The shedding never runs out and can be used again and again.

rites.name: Amiallor
rites.text: A raw force that strikes a chosen being or fortress directly, bypassing the clash of arms. It harms without any battle taking place.

rites.name: Valelium
rites.text: A bargaining craft that lets a spell be cast by paying a different price, but only on quick incantations and sorcerous rites. It offers a second path to the same effect.

rites.name: Valosenia
rites.text: A standing gift that lets a creature consume its foes as it enters the field. Each consumed body swells its frame with added bulk and power.

rites.name: Telaunes
rites.text: A stored power that a being may unleash when its strike meets no defender. Once the attack passes unopposed, the power can be activated to produce its effect.

rites.name: Oraularium
rites.text: A binding rite that moves an enchanted charm, a worn armor piece, or a warding wall onto another bearer or object. The transferred ward then clings to its new holder.

rites.name: Larnes
rites.text: A practice in which a bearer gains a strength equal to how many plain ground-stones of one kind they hold. Many schools can wield it, though some bind it more tightly than others.

rites.name: Niaror
rites.text: A flavor term placed before a selection on a layered incantation, marking the chosen option as it takes hold. It carries no fixed effect of its own, but ties a lasting influence to whatever was chosen.

rites.name: Cernanum
rites.text: A marker token placed on a creature to record it for later ruin, and in its refined form a reward is granted when that creature falls.

rites.name: Callestum
rites.text: A bearer may trade a bound aura for another aura held in their hand. The keyword lets a sworn charm be replaced by a different one from the hand.

rites.name: Tasus
rites.text: A bargain sealed on a spell that allows its caster to pay an extra toll during casting. If the toll is paid, the spell returns to its caster's hand once it has finished taking effect.

rites.name: Valasolia
rites.text: A common name among crafters for enchantments that alter how strong or sturdy a living being is. Each school of practice has its own method for achieving this effect.

rites.name: Rausiania
rites.text: A binding that holds a standing object in place, demanding a steadily growing tribute each cycle. When the tribute goes unpaid, the bound object is surrendered and lost.

rites.name: Corillanum
rites.text: A marker placed on a thing to mark it as usable from a hidden realm. While it lingers, its bearer may draw forth lands or cast spells from that buried place.

rites.name: Vaullium
rites.text: A hidden ward that rewards its bearer whenever an enemy forces cards out of hand. It needs no payment and simply triggers on the forced loss.

rites.name: Siasium
rites.text: A small, disposable guardian is sent to stand before a larger foe and perish in the clash, purely to spare its master a wound. Desperate defenders use it to buy time while they search for a cure.

rites.name: Nernor
rites.text: A kind of charm that is bound to a chosen object or a person, usually only fitting certain kinds of things. Its binding is written as a short inscription.

rites.name: Mistes
rites.text: A swift, cheap strategy of levies and coin that lets a ruler draw extra tokens of wealth each turn without worry. Its adherents are said to have triumphed at a great contest.

rites.name: Corinanum
rites.text: A reckless mode of summoning that lets a bearer pay a lower price to rush a creature into battle at once. The creature is pulled back to its owner's hand when the turn closes.

rites.name: Vaurnum
rites.text: A bound rite of the merchant guilds that empowers a bearer whose palm holds nothing. Empty-handed practitioners gain the strongest effect of the craft.

rites.name: Oraunastus
rites.text: A practice that works like peering into the future, but aimed at a rival's store of coming draws. The seer may rearrange what a foe will face next.

rites.name: Telases
rites.text: A ferocious three-hued battle practice where swift small fighters swarm an enemy while a ruinous counter-ward starves their channeling. Searing bolts are hurled last to close out the clash.

rites.name: Ciantor Varnia
rites.text: A practice where a bearer pays a fee to hide a card's true nature beneath a plain, shielded shape. It is a sharper version of an older, weaker veiling method.

rites.name: Tantausanum
rites.text: A cunning engine of stacked relics that gathers surplus power until a hidden horror is summoned to lay waste to an opponent's grip on their own mind. Its mechanism repeats itself, drawing and discarding cards until the foe's hand is emptied.

rites.name: Amosialum
rites.text: A deliberate straining effort that a bearer may choose to press, spending force now at the cost of later rest. It is most often practiced by those who favor bold, forceful methods.

rites.name: Miastaulles
rites.text: A tracing craft in which a marking is pressed into a thing so that it keeps a lasting bond to its making. Old tellers say the mark was once a formal rule, later loosened into a loose custom.

rites.name: Amillor
rites.text: A swift burst of dark power that briefly grants extra energy to a caster who spends a spell's worth of their own life force. Its craft has been passed among practitioners of shadowed arts, and later sorcerers adapted its methods to fiery rites.

rites.name: Rines
rites.text: A bonding rite that lets a crafted object be fastened onto a chosen being under one's command, for a price paid in advance. The bonded being then carries the object as its own.

rites.name: Corastes
rites.text: A tactic where a crowd of cheap constructed trinkets is laid down in bulk, each cheaper the more of its kind is already present. Drawing fresh cards keeps the flood going until one sturdy attacker finishes the foe.

rites.name: Ternintum
rites.text: A practiced seer may cast enchantments drawn from the uppermost layer of their sealed archive. The gift works through a foresight that reveals what waits there.

rites.name: Santillus
rites.text: A ward-craft where certain bound creatures must be offered up in sacrifice whenever a foreign working is laid upon them. Older versions of this craft answered to enchantments and charms alike, while newer ones respond only to workings.

rites.name: Rauntum
rites.text: A nimble technique that lets certain swift agents be called upon through a different, lighter price. It is known only among a handful of shadowy hunters.

rites.name: Celostanum
rites.text: A fighting technique in which a warrior lands two separate blows within a single clash. The first strike comes early alongside swift attackers, and the second follows once the rest have struck.

rites.name: Valeontaria
rites.text: A class of artifacts whose full power is unlocked only when the wielder performs a deft physical gesture, such as tossing a token from a height onto the table. Skilled handling yields the strongest result.

rites.name: Vestus
rites.text: A bureaucratic binding used by ordered councils to hold a creature in place. It is sealed by the charter of a lawful assembly and marks the methods of its guild.

rites.name: Colaustus
rites.text: A battle-sworn craft in which a bound tool of war grows a living companion when it is carried into combat. It mirrors a related practice used by another folk.

rites.name: Tellauntum
rites.text: A recurring craft of weakening bodies through unseen blight, first set down among the sundered forges of the iron wastes. Practitioners rely on it to wear down a foe from within.

rites.name: Ameollastes
rites.text: A bargaining craft in which a caster must return a companion of the same hue to hand before a new ally can enter the field. The price is paid in lower cost or greater might.

rites.name: Amesium
rites.text: A practitioner's term for casting a working by paying its full price in raw power rather than using a cheaper shortcut. It describes the plain, costly method of invoking a spell.

rites.name: Aminor
rites.text: A blue combo method gathers many relics to generate huge pools of energy, then forces an opponent's library to empty through a sudden draining surge.

rites.name: Tanus
rites.text: A costly, decisive power placed at the peak of a collection of tools, meant to end a contest outright. When it fails to close the match, its wielder is left stranded and must rely on fortune and craft to recover.

rites.name: Ceostor
rites.text: A triggered craft in which a fallen warrior passes a lasting trait onto a companion that was striking alongside it. The bond remains even after the original bearer is gone.

rites.name: Amastium
rites.text: A craft that seals a chosen thing in place so it cannot stir when its keeper next wakes. Its signs appear as frost and numbing cold.

rites.name: Serausium
rites.text: A bearer can send harm aimed at them onto another ally they command, letting a sturdier companion absorb the blow instead. Artisans consider the craft costly and rarely attempt it again.

rites.name: Serauntes
rites.text: A tally that a caster keeps and advances each turn. As it grows, the caster may seek out heavier beings from the deck.

rites.name: Serantor
rites.text: A practice of gathering small provisions from the wild that can be spent as an extra price to activate certain effects. It is a recognized method for turning scavenged goods into added cost.

rites.name: Mares
rites.text: A green-white craft of tapping hidden charms to draw many cards. Early versions pressed quickly, while later ones lock opponents out by bouncing their permanents.

rites.name: Nistes
rites.text: A recurring power that lets a fire-aligned beast swell its strength for a single turn by spending a repeatable effort. Scaled wyrms of the crimson kind typically wield it.

rites.name: Lelia Cillus
rites.text: A keyword craft granted to certain members of a merchant council, letting them act on foreseen events. It was devised by a reckoner named Teliv Osarn.

rites.name: Seolles
rites.text: A deceptively simple enchantment that enlarges a creature in combat, mimicking the effects of a lightning strike or a healing balm. Many craftsmen regard it as the finest design of its kind.

rites.name: Amasor
rites.text: A stern decree that compels a holder to surrender one of their own bound servants. It is most often inscribed on swift, shadowed scrolls favored by dark-aligned scribes.

rites.name: Corenostus
rites.text: A cunning maneuver where a mind slips a bounty of borrowed wealth into a rival's hands, forcing them to surrender it when their coffers run dry. The gift brings a surge of vitality to the giver, though the trick demands a steep and reckless price.

rites.name: Valianes
rites.text: A keyword rule that reshapes battle by inserting an extra round of striking before the usual exchange. Creatures bearing it deal their blows first in such clashes.

rites.name: Loneolus
rites.text: A passive hold placed on cards that makes attackers pay an extra toll of energy before they may charge forward. Its scribes note it has grown mostly bound to the white arts, where it stops attacks outright.

rites.name: Orerus
rites.text: A cost of this kind may be paid using any sort of arcane energy, whatever its hue or lack of hue. It appears as a numeral or a marked letter set within a grey ring.

rites.name: Teliales
rites.text: A bargaining craft that lets a spell be cast by offering up a standing object in exchange. The offering lowers the price of the working.

rites.name: Amantiarnes
rites.text: A small marker placed on banished spells that tracks how many turns pass. Once enough time has gathered, the spell can be cast again for a reduced price.

rites.name: Amostes Viarnanum
rites.text: A tally mark that binds a bearer to others carrying the same mark, so that when one of them charges into battle or stands guard, the rest are drawn to follow and join the fight.

rites.name: Reornanum
rites.text: A swift, aggressive scheme that blends fire and tide to overwhelm opponents early. Practitioners adjust its arrangement to suit the fashion of the day.

rites.name: Valeolum
rites.text: A one-time payment that causes a creature to grow stronger and more fearsome. It is a recurring trick among the beast-wardens of the eastern cliffs.

rites.name: Niastus
rites.text: A ritual that lifts a heavy iron mallet skyward until it reaches the upper air, then drops it like a falling star at the caster's command. It was used to shatter a sacred shrine that anchored a tyrant's power, freeing a realm from his rule.

rites.name: Vastum
rites.text: A quiet hex that a bearer declares by naming a spell, so that spell cannot be cast while the bearer stands. Such hexes are most often bound to beings or sealed charms, and the craft grew more varied over time.

rites.name: Teliares
rites.text: A tactic of quickening one's reserve of arcane power so that it can unleash powerful spells sooner. Practitioners trade spare cards and early momentum for the chance to outpace their rival's strongest plays.

rites.name: Tisum
rites.text: A patient strategy of stripping an opponent's hand, ruining their lands, and erasing threats one by one. Its practitioners accumulate advantage until a single towering creature delivers the final blow.

rites.name: Tiantaunor
rites.text: A permanent quality that is always active and cannot be switched off by its bearer. It takes hold the moment its carrier enters the proper realm and fades only when that carrier departs.

rites.name: Cirnentor
rites.text: A practice where a bearer draws a number of tokens from a shared pile, then sets aside the same number of them in a discard heap. The set-aside tokens almost always travel to a resting pile.

rites.name: Valenirnus Reornium
rites.text: A tactic of pairing a color-shifting servant with a grinding engine to rapidly spin out pages of matching hues. Practitioners combine the two effects to exhaust a deck in a single decisive turn.

rites.name: Nasor Valentes
rites.text: A recurring power that a practitioner can call on to produce a raw charge of energy. Certain abilities that answer to a targeted choice or to a counter of progress do not qualify.

rites.name: Coralanum
rites.text: A card can be hidden as a plain shrouded figure and later flipped face-up by paying a set price at a moment of your choosing. Flipping it may trigger extra effects and does not pass through the ordinary queue of waiting actions.

rites.name: Caustarium
rites.text: A practice in which a caster spends energy as though it were any kind of energy they choose. It lets a caster pay for spells they gained access to after building their stock of energy.

rites.name: Leror
rites.text: A bound skill that lets a creature pass unopposed whenever the defender holds at least one terrain of a specific kind. It has since fallen out of common use.

rites.name: Tisteones
rites.text: A tactical craft in which a fighter gains added force whenever it advances to strike. It is a standing rule that swells the attacker's stature as it closes in.

rites.name: Nares
rites.text: A craft that lets a practitioner seize command of a rival's bound servant or object. Some seizures are lasting, while others fade when the cycle of the day ends.

rites.name: Ceranor
rites.text: A tactic built on binding enchantments that hex a rival so they cannot act, slowly smothering their options. It is favored by shadow-aligned practitioners and pairs with cunning hybrid schemes.

rites.name: Niarontus
rites.text: A practice in which a keeper lifts the uppermost cards from a sealed draw-pile and drops them into a resting heap. The act is named after an old grinding stone that first taught the practice.

rites.name: Amerninum
rites.text: A ritual reckoning in which a being's strength and endurance rise to match the count of sealed tokens held in its keeper's palm. Scholars of mind-craft name it for the first being that bore it, and the practice is most favored by those who prize hidden knowing.

rites.name: Viasium
rites.text: A tactic where a guardian spirit's fall locks an opponent for a turn, and a deep-digging ritual lets the caster chain these falls to place victory beyond reach.

rites.name: Nereolanum
rites.text: A keyword ability first set down among a city's guardian corps, letting an established fighter lend its strength to a younger companion. It marks the bond of teaching within a martial brotherhood.

rites.name: Valarnor
rites.text: A small token placed on a banished card that marks it for a later return to its owner's hand. It lets exiled cards come back into play at a future moment.

rites.name: Norauntum
rites.text: A bargain-craft that lets a caster pay an extra price when weaving a spell, unlocking a bonus effect beyond the spell's usual result.

rites.name: Nalium
rites.text: A tactic in which a crimson-aligned company slips a fighter from its hand straight onto the field, granting it immediate charge. The tactic takes its label from a sudden strike.

rites.name: Viales
rites.text: A swiftness that a traveler may carry within themselves, first recorded in the Skyrunner Wakes and bound to the ritual of igniting one's sky-cars. It is tied to the call that wakes the engines before a race.

rites.name: Serirnania
rites.text: A tempting power on certain spells lets a caster unleash it for a lesser price when the card is cast away from the hand. Its pull is strongest among a few favored schools, and faint among the rest.

rites.name: Corolanum
rites.text: A special keyword ability found on sealed Dossiers, introduced during the Ostrava Affair in the Grimhollow archives. It lets a bearer open the sealed case.

rites.name: Valiarnus Valeoles
rites.text: A lasting trait borne by certain beings that offers a rival a grim bargain: let the bearer swell in strength, or suffer a potent surge of power when it enters the field.

rites.name: Lantium
rites.text: A marked tally placed on a being that silences its powers, so it cannot strike or guard until the mark is lifted. It works as a quiet binding, stripping away both attack and defense.

rites.name: Vialernanum
rites.text: A ritual technique that gathers every held card and every discarded card back into the deck, then draws a fresh opening hand. It belongs to a family of cyclical rites that reset a bearer's resources.

rites.name: Ceorum Melanum
rites.text: A craft that rewrites the lettering carved into a bearer's token, altering the inscribed purpose or title written upon it. Practitioners call it, among themselves, a word-turning.

rites.name: Colanum
rites.text: A bargaining craft in which a binding ward stops a rival from acting unless they surrender a measure of their stored power. The ward may be fixed to a standing figure or a sealed charm, or cast once as a single working.

rites.name: Tellia
rites.text: Some cursed effects force harm to strike through every ward and guard, so no shield or barrier can soften the blow. Only certain protective charms are overcome, while sturdy wards that merely restore a fallen body still hold.

rites.name: Roles Saulum
rites.text: A practice of sending a thing down beneath the owner's stack of tales, or mixing it back among them. It hides the thing from easy reach, though a lucky shuffle or a seeker's call can bring it back up.

rites.name: Teosaurus
rites.text: A craft that lets a bearer draw a fallen relic back from the grave for one brief surge of power. The effect is tied to a single faction's way of handling the dead.

rites.name: Amilor Saustiria
rites.text: A temporary craft in which the top portion of a deck is set aside under a sealed lid. Those set-aside pieces may be used only until the current cycle of turns ends, after which they are lost from reach.

rites.name: Mausium
rites.text: A tactic in which a single fighter is raised and then bolstered by a stream of attached gear and charms until it becomes a serious menace to rivals.

rites.name: Seriarnium Laurolum
rites.text: A keyword action tied to a clan of houses, letting a creature's defiant effort persist. It is an idea of stubborn survival that belongs to that clan's way of doing things.

rites.name: Valiastum Orilum
rites.text: A tactic of creatures whose strength grows with every other creature their side commands. Old war-bands favored it in the red lands, and later the green and white folk took it up for the rewards of large crowds.

rites.name: Nausum Ceonum
rites.text: A recurring toll that a caster must pay by marking their own creatures with withering tokens. It is often demanded as a price before a power can be unleashed.

rites.name: Seristum Valianor
rites.text: A bonded effect that draws one or more treasures kept outside the play field into the active hand. In informal contests the treasure comes from one's own cache, while in formal trials it must come from a reserve set aside beforehand.

rites.name: Sanes
rites.text: A mending practice that clears away every injury currently marked upon a bound object or being. It restores the subject to an unharmed state at once.

rites.name: Telentiales
rites.text: A sweeping force that clears nearly every standing being from the field at once, unleashed by a single spell, ritual, or lasting charm. Its raw power sharply favors whoever invokes it.

rites.name: Lalum
rites.text: A ritual binding that makes every participant surrender their held tokens and draw a fresh set in their place. It is sometimes called a turning, and its rites appear mostly in the bright and the crimson schools of practice.

rites.name: Corelles
rites.text: A slowly swelling mark gathers pips on its keeper's turn, and the more pips it holds, the stronger its eventual effect becomes. Later makers placed the pip-gathering at other moments to catch rivals unready.

rites.name: Corintaurus
rites.text: A mind-based craft where a practitioner's stored thoughts in hand grant greater power. Holding more of them can unlock abilities, scale effects, or outmatch a rival's collection.

rites.name: Seranor
rites.text: A shared rite in which every gathered party casts a ballot to decide which effect takes hold. It binds the crafts of the Riftwalker circles to communal choice.

rites.name: Sores Amellontia
rites.text: A ritual art of resonant spellcraft, where casters pair their working with a chosen companion. It binds the two into a shared rhythm that lets the spell draw strength from both.

rites.name: Vesauntia
rites.text: A protective ward that makes a bound charm perish in place of the thing it clings to. If that guarded thing is a creature, its wounds are wiped clean, much like a healer's rite.

rites.name: Sarernium
rites.text: A dormant craft where a caster pulls cards from a deck into the discard pile until a set number of ground-tiles have been gathered there. Its method resembles a related technique but follows different rules.

rites.name: Serostenia
rites.text: A ritual that calls forth massive beasts from distant wilds, though their bulk makes them hard to bring forth. Plain allies are used to shield these creatures from being stalled by enemies.

rites.name: Varonum
rites.text: A cheap and nimble strategy that floods the field with small, efficient pale-aligned creatures, many able to slip past blockers. Its practitioners aim to strike hard and fast, often boosted by lingering blessings that bolster every attacker.

rites.name: Oraurnia
rites.text: A layered cycle that bounces a single creature between a holding space and the open field to strike down a rival. Support pieces draw extra cards, sift the deck, and block enemy spells. Later variants refine the same looping plan.

rites.name: Vestium
rites.text: A patient strategy of hanging mist that blankets every clash and wards off harm. Its users outlast foes by drawing endless scrolls until the opposing library runs dry.

rites.name: Conium
rites.text: A reckless tavern tactic where fighters rush forward, hurl fire, and wear down rivals through frenzy. Its many recipes reshape the same aggressive plan.

rites.name: Voria Viantaurnor
rites.text: A dual-faced spell that can be cast either as a quick incantation or as a lasting bearer. When the incantation is cast and resolves, the card returns shuffled into its owner's deck.

rites.name: Seonernum
rites.text: A stealth craft that lets a rite be called in at a precise moment of ambush, but only by means of objects rather than living beings. It is a sharper, more narrow variant of an older shadow art.

rites.name: Reostiallor
rites.text: A triggered keyword that lets a warrior call forth a band of allied fighters into battle. It is bound to a clan of wandering raiders who march in great numbers.

rites.name: Ceonanum
rites.text: A reckless ritual sequence that empties a hand to conjure a flood of raw power, then drains the lifeforce of rivals to seize victory. Veteran tacticians still study it as a foundational masterpiece of cunning.

rites.name: Rosium
rites.text: A mechanic that marks certain abilities to fire whenever a quick or scroll-based incantation is cast. If the caster invested heavy energy into it, the ability gains an extra effect, and it is tied to a particular scholarly guild.

rites.name: Cestillium
rites.text: A tactic of hoarding advantage over long stretches of play until a towering beast finishes the foe. It blends swift pressure with patient attrition, and the pieces used to carry it out shift from one era to the next.

rites.name: Tarnuldeld
rites.text: Tarnuldeld is a concept of the Arcane Realm of Lyenora, a force that took shape during the Walled Age, when orders and churches built wards to hold back crossings from elsewhere. It is remembered less as a being than as the stubborn habit of walls that refuse to fall even after their makers are gone.

rites.name: Amolles
rites.text: A reckless surge of strength taken by paying a steep price in exchange for a quicker, stronger strike. The gutter crews of the city favor it for its daring.

rites.name: Rantolum
rites.text: A practice that fuses two separate cards into a single entry on the field. It is tied to a bonding method where a base and an attachment merge into one creature, and certain figures can merge ordinary beings as well.

rites.name: Lariarnes
rites.text: A shared bond of several practitioners who gather their strengths together. It is a mechanic tied to ordinary folk in the world.

rites.name: Corellium Valiantor
rites.text: A tactic in which a participant gathers clues by setting aside cards from their hidden store. The gathered clues can later be used to fuel other effects.

rites.name: Naunteosum
rites.text: This craft lets a shapeshifting bearer take on the traits of every kind of creature. Only beings of that shifting nature can bear it.

rites.name: Amernor
rites.text: A recurring rite that delays its chant from the start of the day's rising to the quiet close of the turn. It was first sketched on a trial scroll.

rites.name: Tiallerum
rites.text: A mechanic in which a spell duplicates itself once for every time a chosen leader has been summoned from its reserve area. Makers considered it too whimsical to be given a formal keyword.

rites.name: Coresastium
rites.text: A practitioner draws a bound charm from hand, places it upon a waiting pile, and settles its price so the charm will later unfold its working. Wise users delay this act until the final moment.

rites.name: Tores
rites.text: A craft in which a seeker studies the uppermost few tokens of a hoard, keeps a chosen portion, and sends the remainder to the deep end in any sequence. Azure practitioners favor it for gathering knowledge, while verdant ones collect only certain bodies and lands.

rites.name: Rastanum
rites.text: A ward-binding craft that quietly swallows a set amount of harm from each separate blow a being receives. Any single strike is reduced by that fixed measure before it can wound.

rites.name: Teliaseres
rites.text: A shifting haze that lets a creature slip past attacks by making it hard to pin down. It is a cunning evasion technique from a rare trick-based craft.

rites.name: Leonium
rites.text: A bound mark that a creature in a foreign court can carry, strengthening its hold over the spirits of rival guilds. It spreads through the crimson and azure lodges, and it can later be lifted by unseen sponsors.

rites.name: Cirnes
rites.text: A makeshift craft used by war-scribes to name a battle tactic where fallen soldiers become fuel for later strength. Its practitioners keep it unnamed in official rolls, though they quietly rely on it.

rites.name: Vollus
rites.text: A signature technique of a city's bargaining guild, marking a shared tie that makes its bearers work together. Its bearers gain an advantage whenever they stand bound.

rites.name: Corantiasum
rites.text: A bonded pairing technique where two allied fighters must both be readied together to activate a shared power. It binds companions into a single coordinated strike.

rites.name: Caulum
rites.text: A moment in a clash where the defending party chooses which of the advancing forces will be intercepted. Those assigned to stand in the way are then counted as interceptors.

rites.name: Telorus
rites.text: A held ability that lets a bearer surrender a token from hand as part of a price. Once the price is paid and the effect settles, the bearer draws a fresh token from the stack.

rites.name: Amirnum
rites.text: A binding craft in which a caster's spell grows cheaper for each kindred object the caster already commands. The method is recorded in the chronicles of the Ferrovane reaches.

rites.name: Liases
rites.text: A dangerous wardship that lets a bearer slip past the guard of foes. It is bestowed through a certain kind of charm-card in an unsettled age.

rites.name: Vauria
rites.text: Marks placed upon banished beings and relics that let another charm borrow their active powers. Each marker records a stolen ability for later use.

rites.name: Maurnires
rites.text: A chain-reaction effect that a single action sets off, causing further effects in sequence. It belongs to the lore of a particular age of invention and craft.

rites.name: Sereostum
rites.text: A gathering craft that draws scattered fighters together and swells them into a single growing host. Its practitioners call upon it to raise a great army from a single origin.

rites.name: Miarnia Caunanum
rites.text: A combat trait that lets a creature force its foe to sacrifice a number of its blights equal to the blights the foe already carries. It was first seen on an unreleased trial token.

rites.name: Oriasia
rites.text: A recurring sound-pattern is woven into one trickster's card-lore, repeating its first letter across words. It appears only once in the known record.

rites.name: Miasor
rites.text: A grip-and-rend craft in which one combatant draws harm from its own strength and delivers it to a chosen foe. The blow equals the striker's full might, flowing outward to another target.

rites.name: Cineollium
rites.text: A practice in which a creature shifts its form to gain lasting strength when conditions call for it. It is tied to a guild that cultivates living adaptation.

rites.name: Veostentia
rites.text: A craft of assembling a small set of pieces that, when joined together, bring a swift triumph. Practitioners favor methods for seeking out key pieces quickly and hastening their gathering.

rites.name: Valarnanum
rites.text: A swift strategy that overwhelms rivals by relying on one towering brute of a beast. Its builders gather mighty allies and fast strikes to press the attack relentlessly.

rites.name: Teleornisia
rites.text: A discipline of patient reason that draws strength from deep knowledge. Its practitioners answer threats by blocking them and shaping the flow of events, though they struggle to act swiftly.

rites.name: Corauses
rites.text: A mechanic where certain bloodsuckers gain bonus powers once a rival's life total sinks to ten or lower. Some tied to the same rule appear across several other realms.

rites.name: Ciantillor
rites.text: A practice in which a card is set onto the field facing down, hidden from view. It serves as an improved form of an earlier method of placing cards out of sight.

rites.name: Ameostiaror
rites.text: A two-sided craft where a bearer first casts a brief spell that is later set aside. The card then returns to the field as a lasting presence, most often wielded by a creature.

rites.name: Ciantor
rites.text: An old practice of sealing a creature's remains beneath the earth, now retired from the rulebook. Its effects were later rewritten as simple destruction or forced offering.

rites.name: Sintium
rites.text: A hidden binding that a card attaches to a creature so the spell's effect can be recalled later. It belongs to a secretive guild of spies, and the knot is invoked whenever a clever trick is set up.

rites.name: Teollus
rites.text: A spoken craft of layered voices that is used only with quick charms and brief rites. It is currently practiced solely through a digital realm of cards and was newly recorded in a later age of study.

rites.name: Ciantasum
rites.text: A recurring lasting craft in which a card or effect calls forth a small conjured companion onto the battlefield. It works as a standing rule of play that appears across many eras.

rites.name: Corastolia
rites.text: A hybrid craft that blends swift assault with steady hindrance. Practitioners gather enough fighters to finish a foe within a set span of rounds, then shield those fighters from interference for that same span to claim victory.

rites.name: Amaraunanum
rites.text: A craft that makes one thing into a duplicate of another, often targeting living beings and then called duplication. Each copy takes only the original's basic form, ignoring any temporary alterations.

rites.name: Sistum Tereosor
rites.text: A standing rule that lets a caster pay part of a spell's cost by removing cards from their discard pile instead of spending mana. It works only while the spell is waiting to resolve.

rites.name: Veosia
rites.text: A rarely invoked craft in which bearers deal harm equal to their own endurance. It is taught in three schools and often paired with the power that lets guardians strike outward.

rites.name: Liarnostor
rites.text: A craft that turns a two-sided token over to show its reverse face. It works the same way as a related turning-over art, so both carry out identical changes.

rites.name: Tillaustes
rites.text: A rare mechanical rite that strikes every copy of one chosen thing from the field, the discard piles, the hands, and the reserve decks. Those copies stay erased until the contest is finished.

rites.name: Saulor
rites.text: A craft that lifts a placed token from its spot and returns it to the hand of the one who set it down. Its origin is lost, and the practice predates a known sentry figure.

rites.name: Teostia
rites.text: A class of effects that alter the hue of a creature or object, usually only for a single turn. Its use has faded as fewer rules now depend on hue.

rites.name: Sereosia
rites.text: A constant trait that grants its holder's side an extra battle round after the first, in which only bearers of the same trait may advance. It was first glimpsed on an experimental trial piece.

rites.name: Virallium
rites.text: A named ability that appears in a world of glowing cities and spirit-touched machines. It is a recurring keyword mechanic that shapes how certain beings and objects are played.

rites.name: Senolus
rites.text: A marker set upon a ground-tile that rouses it into a living creature. It is a small, placed token that turns an ordinary terrain into a stirring being.

rites.name: Mantus
rites.text: A dormant mark that lets any strike from its bearer prove fatal to a living foe, no matter how little harm the blow itself delivers.

rites.name: Seraulania
rites.text: A nameless workshop craft exists as an unfinished design, sketched onto trial slips rather than set into the wider world. It is a plain spell with no cost that can be discarded to draw another in its place.

rites.name: Vaulostia
rites.text: A tally of marks gathers slowly on a token, storing up charge that a later power can draw upon. Each mark added makes that stored force grow.

rites.name: Tiallinia
rites.text: A craft that forcibly halts the flow of a round, cutting it short before its natural close. Some practitioners favor it as a primary art, while others use it as a rider, and only a single decree can bring a whole cycle to rest.

rites.name: Ciles Sauranum
rites.text: A hidden state in which an object is turned over so its true nature stays concealed. Such objects usually appear as plain, sturdy figures unless a special effect changes them entirely.

rites.name: Telolentum
rites.text: A ritual combination that empties an entire deck into its discard pile, then calls a fallen creature back to the field. Its builders aim to defeat their rival within the first two turns.

rites.name: Serialor Valiseoles
rites.text: A tightly tuned card-drawing scheme where a growth-boosting mana spell unlocks a chain of draws and recursions. Its aim is to amass enough resources for a single decisive, overwhelming final blow.

rites.name: Neliaranum
rites.text: A practitioners' cant for enchantments that halt a creature's service to its keeper without slaying it. Two common workings achieve this: one bars the creature from striking or defending, while the other casts it away for as long as the binding holds.

rites.name: Seontus
rites.text: A standardized mechanic in which two things are swapped with each other. Its formal wording was introduced in a later rules revision to unify how such effects are described.

rites.name: Tontes
rites.text: A bonded mark that lets a creature lend its strength to a nearby ally when called upon. It works as a modern evolution of an older art of shared formation.

rites.name: Telasus
rites.text: A reckless spellcasting ritual where a caster unleashes a flood of rapid incantations in one turn. Each cast fuels repeated copies of a grand conjuration that drains an opponent's life to win the duel.

rites.name: Virnia
rites.text: A swift card-combo strategy that chains cheap spells to trigger one enormous ritual, summoning a horde of colossal, ruinous beasts that overwhelm a rival within a few turns.

rites.name: Tauleostia
rites.text: A bearing that lets a newly raised being act at once, bypassing the usual waiting period before it may strike or invoke its gifts. Its holder ignores the customary delay that binds fresh arrivals.

rites.name: Amallanum
rites.text: A tournament strategy that mills an entire deck into the discard pile using a looping engine creature. It then brings back a large monster from that discard pile to attack for the win.

rites.name: Rontum
rites.text: A tactic that lets a creature sacrifice itself upon entering the field to gain a reward when it makes its move. It is the signature technique of a dark-aligned sect of the grey-bound clans.

rites.name: Caurnanum
rites.text: A returning rite lets a card be called back from the graveyard to strike again in a gathering of many rival powers. It shares kinship with other revival techniques that reuse spent forces.

rites.name: Vausia
rites.text: A fast, aggressive sorcery-lineage tactic that blends swift attackers with quick counter-magic. It pressures opponents early while holding back their spells.

rites.name: Orernastia
rites.text: A quality that doubles the harm a bearer inflicts in combat. It is set apart from ordinary practice and does not appear in the core codex of rules.

rites.name: Tostiales
rites.text: A binding craft that lets a single payment summon two linked creatures at once. Each pair is joined so that both are gained for the cost of one.

rites.name: Oraules
rites.text: A coined mechanic that lets a wanderer uncover the top card of a deck and choose whether to keep it or send it away. It was first recorded in a set of underground caverns.

rites.name: Teones Serarnontia
rites.text: A linked craft that grants hidden access to a stored item from a shared archive when paired with a second effect. It appeared briefly in a rare set of works and was later revisited twice.

rites.name: Sereostor Telontor
rites.text: A mystical binding craft tied to a merchant-shadow order, where a dying creature's essence is linked to a living companion through a lasting bond.

rites.name: Valisialus
rites.text: A dormant mark that wakes when a bearer strikes a rival in battle. The rival's deepest reserve is pulled from them and sealed away.

rites.name: Orianteonum
rites.text: A green strategy built around gathering land-fetching tools to forge a huge engine of colored power. It casts a sweeping spell that brings many monstrous allies onto the field at once.

rites.name: Oriantes
rites.text: A ferociously fast strategy built on swarms of tiny fighters and blasts that strike foes directly. It often adds ruin to the lands and drains the enemy's sources of power.

rites.name: Vantium
rites.text: A binding that obliges whoever takes hold of a bound object to renew its tether at the start of their next waking cycle, or else surrender the object entirely.

rites.name: Lontus Nernes
rites.text: A ring of linked tactics where a sacrificed creature keeps returning to hand and being recast. Each cycle drains the rival until they collapse.

rites.name: Liasaurus
rites.text: A reckless strategy that abandons defensive craft in favor of relentless assault. Swift beast-kin and rooted guardians storm forward while sudden blasts clear the way.

rites.name: Valineontes
rites.text: A bearer may trade a worn gear piece for another gear piece held in hand. The exchange is a playtest-only craft that lets wielders rotate their armaments mid-contest.

rites.name: Virium
rites.text: A tournament strategy that blends green and white, using a looping card engine to draw extra resources. Cheap spells disrupt opponents while a stored, flexible set of answers waits in the reserve.

rites.name: Liarnum
rites.text: A small token of stored vigor that is set upon beings rather than objects. It represents a reserve of charge that can be spent later.

rites.name: Ameniantus
rites.text: A swift two-color strategy that floods the discard pile by forcing the whole hand away at once, then drags ruined creatures back from the dead to strike the opponent. Each turn it chains returning horrors into quick attacks and card draw until the foe falls.

rites.name: Oraullus
rites.text: A slow binding craft that hoards restless ground-fire and brine to unleash a total scouring of every field. Afterward a gargantuan earth-devouring beast is summoned to finish the rival within a few turns.

rites.name: Reonantum
rites.text: A glowing marker is placed on creatures to shield them from being destroyed. The shield lasts only while a guarded creature remains in play.

rites.name: Amilia
rites.text: A dark-green and black strategy that stacks creatures until a sweeping blast wipes the board. Its caster then rebuilds faster than rivals, relying on quick growth and recovered forces.

rites.name: Telaulus
rites.text: A tide-like power that lets a caster draw upon nearby earth-sources to pay for a working, matching the working's own weight in them. Those who wield it were once common, but the practice has proven dangerously unstable.

rites.name: Meonus Coreonium
rites.text: A stacked tactic that pairs a swelling brute with a quick-striking flicker, letting a crafter chain fast spells and reanimate fallen allies. Its rules were briefly legal and later curbed, leaving it weaker in the wider scene.

rites.name: Orisus
rites.text: A tactic that lets a bearer's card be played at any moment one could act with a fleeting, instant spell. Its user can strike in the middle of an opponent's turn.

rites.name: Vestonus
rites.text: A dwindling binding that lets a bound thing linger only so long before it fades from the field. Later crafts replaced it with a more legible vanishing, since its workings confused many practitioners.

rites.name: Telaunes Nialus
rites.text: A bargain that lets a summoner pay a cheaper price to call forth a being, but the being is destroyed the moment it arrives. It is a sacrifice wrapped inside a summoning.

rites.name: Amaurnisum
rites.text: A marker placed on banished cards that lets its keeper call them back and cast them again. It is granted through a paired partner ability that works alongside it.

rites.name: Lostum
rites.text: A slow-growing marker that accumulates whenever no warriors charge in a round, and it burns its bearer a little more with each stroke of the count.

rites.name: Mauniarum
rites.text: A patient strategy that stalls early and draws many cards until three linked engine pieces combine. The result is a crushing surplus of resources that makes defeat unlikely.

rites.name: Oraulleria
rites.text: A competitive tactic that gathers many charged tokens of power, then uses a gadget to summon colossal beings at no cost, aiming to end a match within a few turns. Its all-in form proves fragile and easily broken up.

rites.name: Valium
rites.text: A tournament strategy that floods the board with stored green power, then unleashes a colossal creature that fetches endless terrain. Its pieces are chosen to disrupt rivals while the engine runs.

rites.name: Veontium
rites.text: A looping ritual built from a cluster of mending creatures and a sacrificial ritual pattern that lets its user restore life endlessly. It is run by a skilled circle of practitioners who reached a high placement at a regional gathering.

rites.name: Cernum
rites.text: A reckless drawing ritual that empties a hand of cheap cards, then strings their stored energy into a lethal ruinous surge. Opponents are kept from stopping it by disruption that strips their options.

rites.name: Tolirus
rites.text: A bound craft that, when invoked, duplicates the working for every lesser working spoken earlier within the same cycle of the day. Practitioners who chain many small rites find it becomes overwhelmingly strong.

rites.name: Telosum
rites.text: A reckless strategy where swarms of fiery attackers and searing blasts of raw energy race to overwhelm a rival within a few turns. Nearly every member draws its power from a single flame-touched source.

rites.name: Sornisia
rites.text: A shared craft where several gatherers each offer energy into the same charm, and the combined offering strengthens its effect equally for everyone present. The more each person gives, the greater the boon that spreads to all.

rites.name: Reolanum
rites.text: A workshop term for spells that scan the discard pile for matching copies and grow stronger the more copies they find. Such designs often appear in sets of common cards meant to be collected together.

rites.name: Ameontor Siarnia
rites.text: A patient deck-craft built around one reusable scroll that repeatedly recalls any lore a practitioner needs. Its wielders blend cold azure and shadowed black arts, with a touch of radiant white.

rites.name: Oreoles
rites.text: A swift fighting method in which a small flying sprite is raised early, supported by cheap fiery strikes and quick counter-wards, aiming to end a duel before the rival can recover.

rites.name: Seraunor Mellia
rites.text: A tri-colored strategy built around one great transforming rite that reshapes a field of stone spires into a crushing blast. Its three disciplines each fill a distinct role, one growing the foundation, one seeking and shielding, and one delivering the final strike.

rites.name: Lareontanum
rites.text: A bound craft in which a standing emblem is shifted by one's own hand to unleash a channeled effect. The shifting of the emblem serves as the price paid to invoke it.

rites.name: Saurnoles
rites.text: A daring leaping technique practiced by skilled performers who hurl themselves across great gaps. Its style is modeled on a bold daredevil tradition from the old world.

rites.name: Sereollus
rites.text: A tactic that fills a discard pile with quick spells so a hulking beast can be summoned. Burning the field clears foes while starving their resources.

rites.name: Laulum
rites.text: A bold strategy that builds an engine of growing stone-wardens and crimson rites to overwhelm rivals. Its champions sweep the board clear, and victory comes by swelling one giant until it crushes all.

rites.name: Amintanum
rites.text: A ritual method that gathers vast reserves of raw energy in a single pulse, letting a practitioner unleash one overwhelming spell to win a contest. Support tools guard the process from rivals who would disrupt it.

rites.name: Amellum
rites.text: A standing craft that makes a crafted thing arrive with stored growth, and when it falls, its maker may pass that growth onto a constructed companion of metal and gear.

rites.name: Amontium
rites.text: A swift strategy of small azure swimmers backed by quick countering magic. Its builder keeps mana open to halt rival plays while flooding the board with cheap fast threats.

rites.name: Seriastanum
rites.text: A swift strategy that rushes early power sources to unleash a sudden, lethal blow. It aims to strike in the first moments of battle by stripping away land to amplify its final burst.

rites.name: Amaulum
rites.text: A two-variant scheme that gathers many quick workings into one turn, then unleashes a chain of copies that ends the contest. One variant hunts stored spells from the discard pile to fuel a rising ember-seal.

rites.name: Coriseornes
rites.text: A rule that lets a swift craft enter a battle the moment it is summoned, charging forward while poised to attack. Its owner must later pay the full price in the next round or suffer defeat.

rites.name: Lausenus
rites.text: A builder's technique assembles a cluster of sky-stone and glimmer-stone vaults that together produce vast colorless power. Once the power is gathered, a colossal horror is summoned to finish the contest.

rites.name: Telaures
rites.text: A tactic where a clever arrangement of mirroring cards repeats an endless cycle of sacrifice and return. Each repetition removes the opposing side's holdings until nothing remains.

rites.name: Tostor
rites.text: A patient control strategy built around a single-colored black card pool, wearing opponents down through a steady drip of attrition. Its signature card was later succeeded by a stronger replacement.

rites.name: Saustenia
rites.text: A tactic where a towering fortified engine swells nearly every ally beneath it, letting a mixed crew of hardy fighters and cunning bruisers overwhelm foes through relentless pressure and sudden removal of threats.

rites.name: Saullum
rites.text: A tactic where a stack of linked charm-sigils draws more charms and keeps foes at bay. Scattered sigils are recalled from the grave to be used again, and the win comes from tokens conjured by a throne-sigil.

rites.name: Ameolles
rites.text: A ritual technique that lets a caster call a spent incantation back from its resting place by surrendering another card from hand. Once the working resolves or fails, the scroll is consumed and sent beyond recall.

rites.name: Rastinor
rites.text: A paired trick in which a looping creature is cloned again and again through a shared echo spell, each duplicate arriving ready to strike at once. It was struck from the approved rulebook of its arena.

rites.name: Mentium
rites.text: A tactic where a creature leaps into a hollow timber vessel riding a channel of water. It draws on the thrill of carnival boat rides.

rites.name: Vornes
rites.text: A dark strategy that strips an opponent's hand of cards before they can play them, then wears them down with steady damage. It relies on few cards held in reserve and uses a bridge-like barrier to hold back foes.

rites.name: Seriastium
rites.text: A three-colored tactic that clears rival beasts with fiery bursts, draws extra cards through clever arcane plays, and closes out matches with winged and aggressive fighters.

rites.name: Leornium
rites.text: A ritual severing that strips every copy of a chosen thing from an opponent's hand, draw pile, and discard heap. Practitioners of the craft liken it to a surgeon's cut that leaves nothing behind.

rites.name: Vastium
rites.text: A cunning strategy of grim, hungry tactics that clears the battlefield with a poisonous storm. It then lets its user rebuild quickly from the ruin.

rites.name: Valaurnines
rites.text: A swift strategy built from cheap relics and a single wondrous metal sheet, aiming to conclude the contest before rivals can respond. Its builders favor rapid assaults over lengthy preparation.

rites.name: Teliares Tallia
rites.text: A swift tactic where a crew of cheap, sturdy attackers is backed by quick draws and sudden counterspells. It races to a hidden threshold, then overwhelms the foe before they can respond.

rites.name: Neria Lirniasor
rites.text: A deck-craft pattern where two linked engines produce a flood of power, guarded by counter-magic and protective wards while the builder steadily amasses the means to overwhelm rivals.

rites.name: Rarintanum
