rites.text: A dramatic craft that lets a mighty incantation be woven for a reduced price, but only when it is the first thing a caster draws in a given turn.

rites.name: Testum
rites.text: A held breath that freezes every object on the field while a certain spell waits unresolved. It returns later, carried by a blade that brings death.

rites.name: Valeolia
rites.text: A tactic that grows a shadowy force by deliberately wearing down the practitioner's own vitality. It spread from a newer proving ground into an older, long-established one.

rites.name: Teliasia Rantus
rites.text: A controlling plan that uses a temporary token to transform into one enormous creature. Its targets are hard to remove and strike quickly, while spells guard the transformation.

rites.name: Coreostarus
rites.text: A solitary craft in which a lone creature grows stronger when it stands alone among its allies. It stands as the reverse of paired bonds, and its devotees have found it rarely embraced.

rites.name: Valornanum Miror
rites.text: A signature craft that lets a thing be empowered by the colors it has gathered. Its first trial met poor reception, and a later reworking tried to fix it.

rites.name: Meror
rites.text: A practice where a caster arranges to have the right wellsprings of power available so that the spells held in hand can be cast. It is a way of planning which sources are readied before the spells are drawn.

rites.name: Teliantanum Colirum
rites.text: A ritual call that stirs swift travel. It is tied to velocity and drives a rush of motion among the bearers who speak it.

rites.name: Valenarnes
rites.text: A stilling art in which a foe is frozen from striking or guarding while the bearer keeps a steady, direct regard upon them. It resembles a binding craft but cannot halt the foe's special gifts, and it lasts for an unsettled span.

rites.name: Selum
rites.text: A tactic granted to certain creatures that lets them push through defenders when they are the one being guarded against. It works like a sweeping charge, spreading excess force past a blocker's position.

rites.name: Ronia
rites.text: A ritual craft in which a bound object is exchanged for a living being from its owner's household. It can only be performed while the bound object rests in plain view, and the exchange is rarely repeated.

rites.name: Coreosaunes
rites.text: A marker placed on a bound object that keeps it from being readied again. While it lingers, a fastened thing stays bound and cannot return to its ready state.

rites.name: Amornium
rites.text: A rule lets a charging attacker push excess force past a blocker, so leftover harm reaches whatever stands behind the shield wall during the strike phase.

rites.name: Ameolaustus
rites.text: A keyword ability that belongs to a set of cards tied to one shadowy guild. It is an ability cards carry within that block's design.

rites.name: Celia Lontium
rites.text: A bargain-craft where a spell may be cast for a lower price if an ally first casts another spell alongside it. The cheaper cost depends on that paired casting.

rites.name: Valorium
rites.text: A craft that lets a two-sided token be flipped over onto its reverse face, so that a different image and set of properties becomes the one showing. The change happens in an instant and alters what the bearer can see and do.

rites.name: Vintonus
rites.text: A coined craft that turns a bearer into a new shape with set strength and form. It is mainly practiced by one school of arcane artisans who favor cool, blue-tinted working.

rites.name: Valesanum Neosus
rites.text: A practiced technique in which a caster lends nudges of growing strength to allies or to their own creatures, placing small tokens that enlarge them.

rites.name: Lanus Mellistum
rites.text: A standing trait that lets a creature carry several venom tokens at once. It serves as a refined version of an older toxin rule and stands in for a former corruption mechanic.

rites.name: Maules
rites.text: A quality that leaves a bearer open to being struck head-on, as though it stood like a commander exposed on the field. Opponents may choose to force a clash against it directly, bypassing its protectors.

rites.name: Miriastia
rites.text: A lingering resilience that keeps certain beings alive through a cursed dwelling's horrors. It binds closely to those who endure its ordeals and to the hardy lineage that shares their fate.

rites.name: Saunteonia
rites.text: A dormant craft that awakens a bearer's gifts once their stores of spent relics pile high enough. Its unlocked powers grow only when the bearer has gathered seven or more discarded keepsakes.

rites.name: Amolus
rites.text: A marked creature is branded with a hostile designation that makes others more eager to strike at it. Those bearing the mark draw attacks toward themselves.

rites.name: Taullus
rites.text: A bonus that a contender receives in the following round after having lost an earlier round in the same contest. It was first revealed on a trial piece of a sample set.

rites.name: Amianus Corum
rites.text: A binding craft that caps how long a bound object may linger in the world, counting down its stay until it fades away. It is the mirror image of a practice that holds things back until their hour arrives.

rites.name: Telus
rites.text: A standing bond of varied kinds that a holder counts among their allied beings, excluding one dominant hive-kind. Its strength grows with every distinct kind gathered under the bond.

rites.name: Valeorus
rites.text: A fast trick-and-swell tactic where a cheap spell copies a looming beast that grows from every card discarded. Its sudden power fades once the rules are tightened.

rites.name: Telastes
rites.text: A ritual that animates a chosen ground into a temporary guardian that charges forward at once. Its strength grows with stored counters, and when it falls it returns to rest in a dormant state.

rites.name: Lialastor
rites.text: A transit art where a caster pays an alternate price to call a spent incantation back from the discard pile and cast it once more. The cost is paid in a different currency than the usual one.

rites.name: Valaulum
rites.text: A deck built to unleash a chance-driven effect during play. The idea was first tested on a single trial card within a sealed bundle of surprise cards.

rites.name: Voriarnus
rites.text: A keyword action that sends a chosen object into exile, where its owner may later pay a fee to recast it. It mirrors a wind-guided art of gentle removal and return.

rites.name: Lirnes
rites.text: A keyword action that rises from a drifting current, carrying a rival mind's hostile pull across the realm. It is shaped by a designer's hand within an unstable world.

rites.name: Laurniales
rites.text: A combat gift that lets a fighter direct its strikes past any defender that tries to stand in its way. Among the green-kin it was once called by a rougher nickname, Brute Passage.

rites.name: Amenum
rites.text: A ward-mark carved into a bearer's weapon. Each time the mark strikes a foe, its wielder calls forth that many small shades of the same kind and hue to serve beside them.

rites.name: Taules
rites.text: A renewing act performed at the start of each cycle, when a bound object is turned back upright and made ready for use again. It restores what was spent during the previous round.

rites.name: Leornes
rites.text: A recurring trait that a bearer may draw upon once when it falls, returning briefly to the field with an added charge of power.

rites.name: Solanus
rites.text: A tricky combo plan that aims to win by emptying an opponent's library. It relies on a flood of card-drawing spells and a cloud of cheap magic to set the grinding pace.

rites.name: Mollases
rites.text: A hidden trigger that fires from any place a card rests, without being shown to opponents or placed on the waiting line. The effect stays concealed until the moment it resolves, so the card's purpose remains unseen beforehand.

rites.name: Rantelanum Niarnium
rites.text: A tightly built combo-control strategy that gathers unlimited mana of any hue from a rare floating gem, then reuses a trap-like device to draw cards, bounce every enemy threat, or burn the opponent out.

rites.name: Coraullia Leoniarium
rites.text: A growing craft in which practitioners pour ever larger reserves of energy into their workings, and the bound beings respond with greater rewards. It mirrors the way swelling creatures gain strength from their own increase.

rites.name: Sostium
rites.text: A bind that arises whenever a caster must pick one or more options from a set of modes. Choosing among these modes is called facing the bind.

rites.name: Ciareosor
rites.text: A binding practice in which a lasting charm or sigil keeps a being from acting for its keeper without ending its life. Two common forms exist: one silences its strikes and its guard, while the other sends the bound thing away until the sigil is kept in place.

rites.name: Restor
rites.text: A recurring ability word that marks a particular kind of rapid, repeated action. It is bound to a monastic warrior clan that follows a disciplined martial path.

rites.name: Serillum
rites.text: A marker that lingers on a creature and strikes back at a rival when the bearer falls from the field. Bearers can use it to deter enemies from destroying their own or to punish foes.

rites.name: Casiastum
rites.text: A spell in this world has a cost that the caster chooses when declaring it, marked by a placeholder symbol. Most such spells let the caster pay that chosen amount with any color of power, though a few restrict it.

rites.name: Niarnum
rites.text: A deliberate act that turns a sealed passage from barred to open. It is performed upon chambers of a shifting dwelling and only alters whether the way is shut.

rites.name: Nontia
rites.text: A tag-word marking abilities that only take effect when a creature has restored its vitality earlier in the same turn. It belongs to one scholarly circle of herb-learned sorcerers.

rites.name: Seriastor Riasor
rites.text: A patient stalling strategy that freezes the table through locking pieces and counter traps. It bleeds opponents dry by emptying their draw pile while the user quietly restores their own resources.

rites.name: Vanium
rites.text: A fast, all-out strategy that wins by flooding the board with many small summoned creatures. It relies on a handful of spells that keep producing those troops, and it is widely regarded as a serious challenger in its contest.

rites.name: Virernium
rites.text: A tally mark placed on banished spells, counting down each passing turn. Once enough marks gather, the banished spell can be recalled at a reduced cost.

rites.name: Amases Teliarus
rites.text: A keyword that rides along with certain activated effects, showing a bearer unleashing their full strength. It first appeared in a collection of champions from another realm.

rites.name: Valaunarnum
rites.text: A rule where a spell has a base price and several alternative effects, and the caster picks just one effect to pay for when casting it. Each option demands a different amount of energy.

rites.name: Lineornum
rites.text: A tournament strategy that gathers many charged tokens to cast enormous beings at once, aiming to end the contest within a few turns. It is a quick, fragile approach that a single disruption can undo.

rites.name: Sarnauntor
rites.text: A keyword ability that offers an alternative way to pay a cost. Its effect is the same as its counterpart, but it carries a different name depending on the setting.

rites.name: Amernausia
rites.text: A modern combo method that uses a looping spell and token makers to slip a massive creature onto the field early. It rose in popularity after a newly printed, powerful beast became the ideal target.

rites.name: Taraulum
rites.text: A two-card combo craft that once dominated competitive play by creating endless duplicate creatures. The craft was eventually outlawed after its makers overlooked how strong it was.

rites.name: Orenium Vauseornus
rites.text: A tactical strategy built around getting a massive war-hammer into play cheaply, supported by enchanted blades that finish off foes who try to block with fodder. Some versions borrow a few tools from other schools.

rites.name: Teoliror
rites.text: A tag that marks certain effects which awaken whenever a quick incantation is cast aimed at a single being. Scholars of one scholarly guild treat it as their signature art.

rites.name: Tiliantia
rites.text: A fast, aggressive method where a fiery host of cheap attackers swarms early, and searing blasts finish off the foe before the sixth turn.

rites.name: Ameolintor
rites.text: A patient strategy where a band of small wardens rebuilds its ranks after each clash. It overwhelms rival forces by arming, sealing, and sending out steady waves of allies.

rites.name: Oresium Corernanum
rites.text: A tightly built combination strategy that aims to set off a single lasting effect twice in one turn for a crushing blow. It was an early ancestor of a later strategy that dominated its competitive tier.

rites.name: Amares Millor
rites.text: A bending art that lets a practitioner shift the tally of moments attached to their bound tokens. It reshapes how long those tokens endure across the flow of play.

rites.name: Cantiastus
rites.text: A keyword action unique to each set of cosmic gems, tied to the single gem that powers that set. It is used during play to channel the gem's specific force.

rites.name: Tirnellanum
rites.text: A rare and costly craft that forcibly brings a turn to an abrupt close. Practitioners treat it as a fine art, and its use echoes the seizing of an additional turn.

rites.name: Amontesum
rites.text: A recurring craft bound to certain spellcasts, so that its effects echo again each turn for the rest of the match. Lessons teach it to all who study it.

rites.name: Caustes
rites.text: A rare latent gift lies dormant in a few sentient beings across many worlds. When awakened, it lets its bearer cross between those worlds at will, though how it works remains largely unknown.

rites.name: Corellum
rites.text: A keyword ability carried by certain objects that lets them jump across vast distances at speeds beyond light. It marks the sweeping travel of the outer frontier.

rites.name: Sileila
rites.text: Sileila is the concept of a single unwritten thread in Lyenora's Three Futures, the moment the ending forks and the Library must shelve each outcome side by side. It exists as a quiet pressure on which branch becomes real, felt most strongly where arcane powers gather.

rites.name: Suralaruta
rites.text: Suralaruta is a concept of the Lyenora Arcane Realm, a thought-form that takes shape when the Three Futures branch and the Library catalogues each outcome on its shelves. It is bound to the Age of the first sovereign, when groves and growing kingdoms were still the chief marks of settled life.
